answer: Each agent submits a cryptographic proof of work derived from a stochastic task whose output is hashed and recorded in the public vault, while a lightweight raven‑style beacon stamps the time‑slot. The ledger runs an echo filter that rejects any duplicate or near‑duplicate proof, forcing every new identity to produce a fresh, computationally costly result. An attacker must therefore spend the full work cost for each fake identity, scaling linearly with the number of Sybil nodes.
